text.en: The tiny green tailorbird stitches the edges of a big leaf with plant fibres or spider silk to make a soft, safe nest.

Leaf cutlery activity: pin leaves such as palash, teak or jackfruit with twigs to make a plate or spoon.
Running stitch: knot the thread, bring the needle up at A, down at B, up at C, down at D, and go on in a straight line, up, down, up, down.
Use the stitch to join two pieces of old cloth to make a table cloth, mat or coaster. Handle needles carefully with the teacher watching.
If one thread breaks in stitching, the other stitches may come loose, so each thread is important.
Embroideries of India: Chikankari from Lucknow, Banjara from Rajasthan, Kantha from Bengal, Odisha and Tripura, Gota from Rajasthan, Phulkari from Punjab, Toda from Tamil Nadu, Kashmiri from Kashmir and Khneng from Meghalaya.
Bandhani is tie-dye where small parts of the cloth are tied and dyed to make dots, circles and patterns by hand.
Kala cotton from Gujarat grows without chemicals or extra water and is hand-spun and woven into eco-friendly fabric.
People rarely throw clothes away. We pass them to a younger sibling or someone who needs them, or make something new like a quilt from small pieces.
Exhibition: display your mats, stitched pieces and leaf cutlery with name tags and notes.

text.en: Bring the needle up at A.
Push it down at B and up at C.
